question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, immutable `--config-layer` inputs as a permanent core Gateway contract, or require managed hosts to keep composition outside core until a different extension seam is approved?
rationale: Correctness and proof do not decide whether core should own a new public precedence, authority, and immutability model; that choice affects long-term CLI compatibility and hosted deployment architecture.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
options.body: Approve the startup-only design, require a rebase onto the current managed write-owner seam, and complete current-main integration validation before merge.

options.title: Wait for the RFC decision
options.body: Keep the PR open but pause implementation review until the linked managed-configuration RFC fixes the permanent ownership and compatibility contract.

options.title: Keep composition host-side
options.body: Decline the new core CLI surface and require Lobster or other launchers to materialize one validated canonical config until a narrower generic API is justified.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only design, require a rebase onto the current managed write-owner seam, and complete current-main integration validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting product and core-architecture contract rather than a routine file-level repair, and recent history shows direct ownership of Gateway/config integration decisions.
